title: 'Operation Ghostbusters': 5 charged, including 3 from NJ, in alleged financial aid scheme - 6abc Philadelphia
text:
'Operation Ghostbusters': 5 charged, including 3 from NJ, in alleged financial aid scheme - 6abc Philadelphia 
 24/7 Live Philadelphia Pennsylvania New Jersey Delaware Action News Investigation 
 'Operation Ghostbusters': 5 charged in alleged financial aid scheme 
 'Operation Ghostbusters': 5 charged, including 3 from NJ, in alleged financial aid scheme WPVI By Chad Pradelli , Cheryl Mettendorf Wednesday, November 18, 2026 4:39AM Share Follow 6abc on Google Federal prosecutors have charged five people, including three from New Jersey, in what authorities describe as a "ghost student" scheme that allegedly stole millions of dollars in fraudulent college financial aid.
 The charges stem from an investigation dubbed " Operation Ghostbusters ," which targeted individuals accused of using stolen identities to enroll people in colleges without their knowledge, apply for financial aid and collect proceeds from the aid payments.
 One alleged victim, Wisconsin resident Tony Rice, said he discovered earlier this year that a student loan for roughly $10,000 had been opened in his name.
 "I've never been to college a single day in my life," Rice said.
 According to authorities, Rice had apparently been enrolled in classes at Colorado Technical University, located about 1,000 miles from his home.
 "I was actually furious. And see, I get chills just thinking about it," Rice said.
 SEE ALSO | 'Ghost students' stealing millions in college financial aid | Investigation 
 'Ghost students' stealing millions in college financial aid | Investigation 
 Authorities allege that 23-year-old Kenyan national Francis Mogambi enrolled unsuspecting victims such as Rice in college, applied for financial aid and took a portion of the proceeds.
 "The college will take the tuition and fee out of it and then provide the remaining money to ghost students," said Heith Janke, assistant director of the FBI's Criminal Division.
 Janke said investigators believe criminals purchase Social Security numbers and other identifying information on the dark web.
 They then target people who have never attended college and use their information to submit applications through the Free Application for Federal Student Aid, or FAFSA.
 Authorities say so-called money mules open bank accounts to receive illicit proceeds, with much of the money allegedly being sent overseas.

 "We've identified what we believe are over 830,000 fraudulent FAFSA accounts that have been used, and we've seen 130 million associated with those accounts," Janke said.
 An Action News investigation in January found local colleges also had been affected by suspected ghost student activity.
 Delaware County Community College and Community College of Philadelphia each flagged more than 500 suspected ghost student applications in recent years.
 "It really does make you pause and say, 'OK, there's a real problem here, and we need to do something about it,'" said Gina Macklin of Delaware County Community College.
 According to court records, Mogambi's roommate in Lincoln, Nebraska, reported him to authorities.
 Mogambi came to the United States in 2024 after winning the Diversity Visa Lottery, became a permanent resident and, according to the report, also worked as a nursing assistant while allegedly operating the scheme.
 Rice said he faced significant challenges trying to remove the debt and repair his credit, adding that officials did not initially believe he was a victim of identity fraud.
 "For the longest time, they were fully confident, nope, Tony Rice is enrolled. He is trying to go for computer science. He has a loan, and they were taking it very serious until the last leg," Rice said.
 Authorities have charged Mogambi with theft of government money and identity theft.
 He is awaiting federal trial.
 Despite the arrest, Rice said his situation remains unresolved.
 "This started in December, and it's not resolved for me," he said.
 Meanwhile, multiple bills have been introduced in Congress that would strengthen student verification requirements before federal student aid is distributed. None of the proposals have passed so far.
